deals.travelWindow: Sep 9 – Nov 18, Tue/Wed/Sat travel only (blackout Oct 9–14 & Nov 8–11); book the sale fare by tonight 11:59pm ET
deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's fall flash sale has Boston–Denver one-ways at $99 (~$198–250 RT stacking two sale fares), and Rocky Mountain NP is 90 minutes up the road.
deals.soloWhy: LoDo and RiNo are walkable and full of solo diners at the bar, the A Line train runs straight from the airport downtown, and Bear Lake's easy trails make for a low-stakes solo hiking day.

highlights: Union Station's Great Hall for coffee and people-watching
RiNo (River North) street art and brewery row
Denver Art Museum's Indigenous arts wing
Bear Lake Road in Rocky Mountain NP — no permit needed off-season
Cheesman Park at golden hour
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, take the A Line into Union Station, wander LoDo, dinner and a beer flight in RiNo.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the day, drive to Rocky Mountain NP via Estes Park, hike Bear Lake to Nymph and Dream Lake (easy, ~2 mi round trip), sunset over Lake Estes.
Day 3 — Denver Art Museum or Denver Botanic Gardens, browse REI's flagship store, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is walkable and the A Line light rail covers the airport-to-LoDo run with no car needed. Rent a car only for the Rocky Mountain NP day — return it same day to skip overnight parking fees.
guide.stayArea: LoDo or RiNo — both walkable to restaurants and transit, with a livelier bar scene for solo evenings than the suburbs.
food: Avanti Food & Beverage (food hall, good for solo grazing)

deals.travelWindow: Sep 9 – Nov 18, Tue/Wed/Sat travel only (blackout Oct 9–14 & Nov 8–11); book the sale fare by tonight 11:59pm ET
deals.whyRanked: The single cheapest fare in the sale: $104 one-way (~$208–260 RT). No park boost, but it's a legitimate warm-weather escape at the lowest price of the five.
deals.soloWhy: Doable solo but sprawling and car-dependent — better suited to a self-directed sightseeing trip than a walkable city break, and most attractions (theme parks especially) are built for groups.

highlights: Winter Park's Park Avenue and the Scenic Boat Tour
Lake Eola Park at sunset
Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex
Blue Spring State Park manatees (Nov–Mar season)
One theme park day if you want it — Universal's Islands of Adventure works well solo
itinerary: Day 1 — Winter Park: Park Avenue shops, the Scenic Boat Tour on the chain of lakes, dinner nearby.
Day 2 — Day trip east to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (~1 h drive), back for a sunset walk around Lake Eola.
Day 3 — Universal Islands of Adventure (single-rider lines make it easy solo) or a springs day at Blue Spring State Park, then fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Rental car is essential — Orlando has no real transit network and everything is spread across highway exits.
guide.stayArea: Winter Park or the Lake Eola/Downtown Orlando area — walkable and removed from the International Drive tourist strip.

deals.travelWindow: Sep 9 – Nov 18, Tue/Wed/Sat travel only (blackout Oct 9–14 & Nov 8–11); book the sale fare by tonight 11:59pm ET
deals.whyRanked: $119 one-way (~$238–290 RT) for a walkable downtown with live music every night, and Mammoth Cave NP is a 2-hour drive if you want a park day.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown and The Gulch are dense and walkable, the honky-tonks are built for striking up conversation at the bar solo, and there's an easy day-trip menu (Mammoth Cave, Leiper's Fork) if you want a break from the city.

highlights: Broadway honky-tonk crawl (free live music, no cover)
Ryman Auditorium daytime tour
Country Music Hall of Fame
Mammoth Cave NP guided cave tour (book ahead)
East Nashville's coffee shops and vintage stores
itinerary: Day 1 — Broadway honky-tonk crawl, Ryman Auditorium, dinner in The Gulch.
Day 2 — Drive north to Mammoth Cave NP (~2 h) for a ranger-led cave tour, or stay local and do Leiper's Fork village plus the Percy Warner Park trails.
Day 3 — Country Music Hall of Fame, East Nashville coffee and vintage shopping, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown, The Gulch, and East Nashville are walkable or a short rideshare apart. Rent a car only if doing the Mammoth Cave day trip.
guide.stayArea: The Gulch (walkable, quieter at night) or East Nashville (more local, better coffee/food scene).

deals.travelWindow: Sep 9 – Nov 18, Tue/Wed/Sat travel only (blackout Oct 9–14 & Nov 8–11); book the sale fare by tonight 11:59pm ET
deals.whyRanked: $129 one-way (~$258–310 RT) for consistently mild weather, plus Anza-Borrego and Joshua Tree NP both within a couple hours.
deals.soloWhy: Pacific Beach and Little Italy are walkable and hostel-friendly, the trolley covers downtown/Balboa Park/Old Town well, and the desert day trips are easy solo drives with clear trailheads.

highlights: Balboa Park's museum row and botanical building
La Jolla Cove tide pools and sea lions
Sunset Cliffs Natural Park at golden hour
Anza-Borrego badlands and slot canyons
Little Italy's Saturday farmers market
itinerary: Day 1 — Balboa Park museums and gardens, Gaslamp Quarter dinner.
Day 2 — La Jolla Cove in the morning (sea lions, tide pools), Sunset Cliffs at sunset.
Day 3 — Day trip to Anza-Borrego Desert State Park (Slot Canyon, Font's Point) or push further to Joshua Tree NP, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The trolley and bus network covers downtown, Balboa Park, Old Town, and La Jolla reasonably well. Rent a car only for the desert day trip.
guide.stayArea: Little Italy (walkable, good food, close to the airport) or Pacific Beach (beachier, more hostels and solo travelers).

deals.travelWindow: Sep 9 – Nov 18, Tue/Wed/Sat travel only (blackout Oct 9–14 & Nov 8–11); book the sale fare by tonight 11:59pm ET
deals.whyRanked: The priciest of the five at $154 one-way (~$308–360 RT), but it's still a flash-sale fare on a route that normally runs well over $400, and Point Reyes National Seashore is an hour north.
deals.soloWhy: Muni and BART make the whole city reachable without a car, and neighborhoods like the Mission and Hayes Valley are dense enough to wander solo all day without repeating a block.

highlights: Crissy Field and the Golden Gate Bridge walk
Ferry Building Marketplace
Mission District murals and taquerias
Point Reyes Lighthouse and the Point Reyes headlands
Dolores Park on a clear afternoon
itinerary: Day 1 — Crissy Field to the Golden Gate Bridge on foot, Ferry Building Marketplace for lunch.
Day 2 — Mission District mural walk and taquerias, Dolores Park, Haight-Ashbury in the evening.
Day 3 — Day trip to Point Reyes National Seashore (lighthouse, Chimney Rock) or Muir Woods, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Muni and BART cover the city well — skip the rental car except for the Point Reyes/Muir Woods day trip.
guide.stayArea: Hayes Valley or the Mission — both walkable, transit-connected, and closer to the food scene than the Fisherman's Wharf tourist strip.
